entries.concept: Seventeen Atlas force concepts operationalize dimensions of national condition and influence using approved source indicators.
entries.atlas_interpretation: An Atlas operational measurement framework with partial coverage ceilings and explicit unscored dimensions.
entries.framework_differences: The 17 Atlas forces are not a one-to-one quotation of the author's determinants and do not imply the author's approval.
entries.measurement_limitations: Several forces remain context-only or dimension-only; incomplete proxies are never silently treated as complete concepts.

entries.source_title: Big Cycle Atlas experimental cycle classifier
entries.concept: Eight Atlas labels used by the experimental national-condition classifier (including RISE, PEAK and DECLINE variants).
entries.atlas_interpretation: A labelled Atlas operational framework for current/research-state classification only.
entries.framework_differences: Not represented as the author's original stage structure and not a validated long historical Big Cycle stage map.
entries.measurement_limitations: Stage thresholds are sensitivity-tested assumptions; classified periods are retrospective and not release-date-safe.

entries.source_title: Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order: Why Nations Succeed and Fail
entries.source_edition: Avid Reader Press / Simon & Schuster hardcover (ISBN 978-1-9821-6027-2)
entries.chapter_section: Long-term debt/capital-cycle discussion; exact wording and edition context require page-level citation
entries.concept: An approximate roughly-75-year duration is proposed for long debt/capital-cycle dynamics, with substantial variation.
entries.atlas_interpretation: A falsifiable duration hypothesis candidate only. Atlas does not use it to advance stages, produce countdowns or date an order transition.
entries.framework_differences: The claim is not treated as a universal Big Cycle duration and the source context is narrower than a complete civilizational cycle.
entries.measurement_limitations: Atlas lacks independent, consistently dated full cycles and boundary-stable entities needed to estimate duration. No numeric duration estimate is currently defensible.

entries.source_title: Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order: Why Nations Succeed and Fail
entries.source_edition: Avid Reader Press / Simon & Schuster hardcover (ISBN 978-1-9821-6027-2)
entries.chapter_section: Chapter 1, 'The Big Cycle in a Tiny Nutshell'
entries.concept: A broad historical cycle in which monetary, domestic-order and external-order arrangements rise, interact, break down and are replaced.
entries.atlas_interpretation: A research framing for measuring related debt, institutional, international-power and conflict evidence — not a validated stage law.
entries.framework_differences: Atlas separates measured national condition, international power and independent outcomes; it does not adopt a deterministic sequence or calendar advancement.
entries.measurement_limitations: The author's narrative synthesis does not specify a unique dataset, frequency, threshold or falsification rule. Atlas's modern panel is far shorter than the claimed historical cycle.

entries.source_title: Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order: Why Nations Succeed and Fail
entries.source_edition: Avid Reader Press / Simon & Schuster hardcover (ISBN 978-1-9821-6027-2)
entries.chapter_section: Part I, Chapter 6, 'The Big Cycle of External Order and Disorder'
entries.concept: Relative international power, rivalry and order transitions are linked to changes in economic, trade, financial, military and monetary influence.
entries.atlas_interpretation: Atlas publishes separated international-power measures and asks whether convergence predicts independently dated rivalry/crisis events.
entries.framework_differences: Atlas does not combine power dimensions into a leadership ranking or predict a transition date.
entries.measurement_limitations: Reserve shares, international banking, conflict outcomes and pre-1900 entities remain incomplete.

entries.source_title: Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order: Why Nations Succeed and Fail
entries.source_edition: Avid Reader Press / Simon & Schuster hardcover (ISBN 978-1-9821-6027-2)
entries.chapter_section: Part I, Chapter 5, 'The Big Cycle of Internal Order and Disorder'
entries.concept: Internal cohesion, institutional quality, wealth/opportunity gaps and productive capacity strengthen or weaken together over time.
entries.atlas_interpretation: Institutional deterioration is evaluated as a predictor of later investment/productivity weakness, not as a stage countdown.
entries.framework_differences: Atlas currently uses partial WGI, education, inequality and productivity proxies; it does not claim complete institutional measurement.
entries.measurement_limitations: Values gaps, political conflict and structural institutional change are only partially observed; causal attribution remains unsupported.

entries.source_title: Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order: Why Nations Succeed and Fail
entries.source_edition: Avid Reader Press / Simon & Schuster hardcover (ISBN 978-1-9821-6027-2)
entries.chapter_section: Part I, Chapter 3, 'The Big Cycle of Money, Credit, Debt, and Economic Activity'
entries.concept: Debt, credit, money creation and repayment burdens interact over short debt cycles and longer financial/order cycles.
entries.atlas_interpretation: Testable as debt, credit, debt-service, external-position and independently defined crisis relationships at annual/quarterly horizons.
entries.framework_differences: Atlas keeps private debt, public debt and debt-service measures separate and evaluates against independent crisis chronologies.
entries.measurement_limitations: Public-debt and external-debt coverage are incomplete; historical release timing is not yet available for most macro predictors.
